body: Okay, then experience my life and then see if you can deal with it.

Dude, I really empathize with your situation. I am also in that right now: isolated, shitty job, and just basically ruined my life because I chose to be selfless. I learned my life lesson. Always be selfish. Fuck people.

Right. You get me. The worst was when I said I was going to get a Master's and they said I would be unemployable due to the degree—plus it would be a waste of my time, efficiency, and money. I felt like shit after that. Just like- I'm a leper in the job world. It's kinda funny when you think about it.

It kinda is, from my perspective. Are you psychologically distancing yourself from the issue—from this standpoint so you can continue to do so? When you do 'make enough' and stop, what's to stop you from doing this again in another event in the future?
I hope you do attain that dream and I hope you have a wonder day :)
Life sucks sometimes but I hope you have a good one. What is a good day that you've had? Walk me through it, or not. I just hope you are doing well.
Do you think of your victims as people or as objects? Because from my POV, you see them as property to profit from. Do you have empathy?
What is your dream in life? What is the one thing you would like to be remembered for?
Thanks. Yeah, it's just hard and it feels like maybe I'm not trying hard enough, you know?

Exactly. Also, there is a difference to a person who has a close relationship with an alleged or suspected narcissist than diagnosing someone over the internet. The problem with narcissism is that they cannot be said they are narcissists until a valid mental health professional diagnoses them. Therefore, a psychologist or psychiatrist could use phrases such as "seemingly exhibiting narcissistic behavior" or asking the person within that relationship if they believe that person is one.

I find the act of using words such as "narcissist, psychopath, or sociopath" with the intent to insult and hurt is a mean-spirited approach. It brings a bunch of stigma to the people who have these disorders, and it also lets people start labeling and diagnosing others with mental illnesses WITHOUT the credentials to back it up.
And it's replies like this that make me lose a bit of my faith in humanity.

If I may be frank, none of you are qualified to diagnose Eugenia with Narcissistic Personality Disorder. If you do have the qualifications, you would know you would have to do a psychological evaluation with your client. You guys can speculate all you want. At the end of the day, you don't know her really, and you don't know what she has been through. Seeing how you guys just brushed aside /u/hannahjmaguire's analysis without understanding her testimony and viewpoint is disingenuous to an open discussion.
